welcome.title: Welcome to StudyBudget
welcome.subtitle: A money tracker for students abroad: no sign-up, works offline, home and local currencies side by side.

currencies.title: Many currencies, one total
currencies.body: Keep home and local money apart; totals convert to the currency you think in.

card.title: Your home card abroad
card.body: Type what you paid in local currency; the charge including the foreign fee is estimated for you.

budget.title: What’s left this month
budget.body: Set a budget to see what you can spend per day and where the money goes.

private.title: Stays on your phone
private.body: No account, nothing uploaded; just back up now and then.

currencies.title: Where are you studying?
currencies.intro: This is used to suggest your accounts; you can change everything later.
currencies.localHint: For cash and a local bank account.
currencies.homeHint: For your bank account and credit card back home.
currencies.totalsHint: The overview, budgets and account total are converted to this currency. You can change it in Settings.

accounts.title: Which accounts do you use?
accounts.intro: Tick the ones you use. Balances can stay empty; you can set them on the Accounts page later.
accounts.feeHint: What the bank adds when you use this card abroad; 1.5% is typical for Taiwanese cards.

safety.title: Your data stays on this phone
safety.intro: Three things to know before you start.

private.title: No sign-up, nothing uploaded
private.body: Your records live only in this browser; the app only goes online to fetch exchange rates.

backup.title: Back up now and then
backup.body: Clearing browser data or changing phones erases your records. Download a backup from Settings to your cloud drive now and then; you’ll be reminded after 7 days.

install.title: Add it to your home screen
install.body: iPhone: Safari “Share → Add to Home Screen”. Android: Chrome menu “Install app”. It then works offline, and its data is less likely to be cleared.

guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: Everyday situations abroad, and how to record them in StudyBudget.
guide.settingsHint: How to record common situations, like card payments abroad, friends paying you back, and rent.

accounts.title: Accounts and currencies
accounts.body:
Each account has its own currency, such as yen cash or a card billed in TWD. Balances come from your entries; if one doesn’t match your bank app, set the current balance on the Accounts page.
The overview and account total are converted to your main currency, which you can change in Settings.

record.title: Adding an entry
record.body:
Tap “+” in the middle of the bottom bar, pick the account, type the amount, tap a category and save. To enter several in a row, use “Save & add another”.
Places you go often appear under “Frequent” at the top of the form: tap one and only the amount is left. Typing a payee you have used before also picks its usual category.

foreignCard.title: Using your home card abroad
foreignCard.body:
Tap the currency next to the amount and pick the local one (e.g. JPY), then type what you paid. The charge to your card is estimated from exchange rates and the card’s foreign fee, and marked “Est.” in the list.
When the statement arrives, open “N estimates to check” under the card on the Accounts page and enter each actual charge, or tick “Matches the statement”.
The fee stays in the same entry but counts under Fees in the overview. Set the rate on the Accounts page; Taiwanese cards typically charge 1.5%. Each account remembers the currency it last paid in.

refund.title: Friends paying you back, refunds
refund.body: When a friend pays you back for something you covered, choose “Refund” and the category of the original expense (e.g. Dining out). It is taken off that spending instead of counting as income. Store refunds work the same way.

transfer.title: Transfers, cash withdrawals, card payments
transfer.body:
Money moving between your own accounts (money from home, an ATM withdrawal, paying off a card) is a “Transfer”: neither income nor spending.
Across currencies, enter both the amount sent and the amount received to see the rate. A fee can be added too; it is saved as a separate Fees expense.

monthly.title: Rent, subscriptions and other monthly entries
monthly.body:
When adding the entry, open “More” and tick “Repeats monthly”. Each month when it is due, the Transactions page asks you to record or skip it.
In Settings → Monthly entries you can change the amount or day (say, after a price rise) or stop it.

overview.title: What’s left this month
overview.body: Overview converts every currency into your main one: spending this month, what is left of your budget, how much you can spend per day, and which categories the money went to. Tap a category to see its entries.

search.title: Finding old entries
search.body: Tap the magnifier next to the month to search every month by payee, note or category name; the filter button next to it narrows the list to an account or type. To analyse in a spreadsheet, export a CSV in Settings.

backup.title: Backups and new phones
backup.body:
Your data lives only in this browser and is never uploaded. Download a backup from Settings now and then and keep it in your cloud drive; on a new phone, restore it. You are reminded after 7 days without one.
Add the app to your home screen (iPhone: Safari “Share → Add to Home Screen”; Android: Chrome menu “Install app”) so it works offline and the browser is less likely to clear its data.

undo.title: Saved or deleted by mistake?
undo.body: After saving or deleting, “Undo” appears at the bottom of the screen for a few seconds and puts things back. “Save & add another” offers Undo in its message too.
